sentences.text:
Milan Sk vs Unknown on 18 December, 2025
54. 18.12.2025

Court
No.8 (Tanmoy)
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Ia No: Cran/1/2025
 In
 Cra (Db)/396/2025
 In Re: - An application under Section 389 Cr.PC, 1973 / Section
 430 of Bnss, 2023 in connection with the judgment and order
 dated 29/30.7.2025, passed by the learned Additional Sessions
 Judge, Fast Track Court, Berhampore, Murshidaba in St
 No.01/June/2023 corresponding to Sc No. 291/2023 arising
 out of Hariharpara Ps Case No. 262/2020 dated 03.09.2020 and
 convicted under Sections 498A/302/34 of the Indian Penal
 Code, 1860.
 And

In the matter of: - MILAN SK.
 ...applicant/appellant.
 Mr. Ayan Bhattacharya, Sr. Adv.
 ...for the applicant/appellant.
 Mr. Prasun Kumar Dutta, APP  Mr. Ashoke Das  ...for the State.

Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.
1.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased victim.
All other accused persons, being members of the applicant's family, have been acquitted from the charges under Sections 498A/302/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Only the applicant has been convicted under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and has been sentenced to suffer life imprisonment by a judgment and order dated July 29/30, 2025.
He now prays for suspension of sentence pending disposal of the appeal.
2. Learned Counsel for the applicant points out that all the private prosecution witnesses have been declared hostile.
The Autopsy Surgeon was not examined by the prosecution.
There is absolutely no material on the basis of which the learned Trial Court could have convicted the applicant.
3. Learned State Counsel, while opposing the prayer, says that the conviction was based on Section 106 of the Evidence Act.
There is enough material to support the conviction.
It is a case of murder.
No leniency should be shown to the applicant.
4. We find that PW1, being the father of the victim lady and the de facto complainant, has deposed completely against the prosecution case, so has PW2, the mother of the victim lady.

5. Therefore, we find prima facie that the applicant has made out an arguable case.
Accordingly, we allow this application and we hereby do suspend the sentence of imprisonment of the present applicant.

6. It is thus ORDERED that the applicant, namely, MILAN SK., shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), with two sureties of like amount each,
one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Murshidabad at Berhampore,

subject to condition that the applicant, while on bail, shall not leave the geographical limits of the district of Murshidabad without the leave of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Murshidabad at Berhampore and shall report to the Officer-in- Charge/Inspector in-Charge of Hariharpara Police Station once in a month until further orders and that the applicant shall be personally present or be represented by his learned Counsel during hearing of the appeal and he shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.
7. The operation of the order of conviction and sentence shall remain suspended till disposal of the appeal or until further orders, whichever is earlier.

8. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendents of the concerned Correctional Homes for immediate release of the present applicant/ appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

9. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
10. The application being IA No: CRAN/1/2025 is accordingly disposed of.
11. Criminal Section is directed to make available certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance with all requisite formalities.

(Uday Kumar, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
